name: Founding Elders and Chantries of the Pyramid (Libellus Sanguinis II Lore)

text.content: Left to manage the nightly affairs of Clan Tremere's founding chantry at Ceoris while Tremere himself lies in voluntary torpor, Etrius is haunted by the price the clan paid for its immortality. Where Goratrix glories in the transformation from mortal magus to Cainite, Etrius has never stopped mourning it, and his letters to fellow elders dwell openly on the clan's "pitiful half-life" and his private doubts about whether Tremere's amaranth of the Antediluvian Saulot was a triumph or a catastrophic mistake. He was present in the meeting chamber the night Tremere returned from Saulot's haven bearing the power of the third generation and declared the clan "by blood and by destiny" before entering torpor alongside his closest advisors — Etrius, Goratrix, and Meerlinda among them — leaving the Council of Seven to govern in his absence. Decades on, Etrius still broods in Ceoris's library over the fragmentary, contradictory accounts of that night, troubled by dreams he will not fully describe even to his most trusted correspondents, and by a growing suspicion that whatever Tremere sacrificed to found the clan, the price is not yet fully paid.

pages.name: Goratrix, Architect of the Great Working

text.content: Where Etrius mourns, Goratrix exults. As the chief instigator of the ritual that transformed House Tremere's mortal magi into the vampires who would found the clan, Goratrix regards the loss of True Magick as a fair trade for what he considers a transformation beyond mortal imagining, and he has little patience for what he calls Etrius's "constant moaning." Established in his own chantry in France, Goratrix pursues alchemical and magical experimentation on captive subjects he refers to, without apparent irony, as his "toys" — work that has made the clan enemies among the Gangrel (whose kind he used to create his Gargoyle servitors) and the Nosferatu alike. His growing infernal sympathies and increasingly open contempt for other clans presage his eventual fall: within House Tremere's internal politics he already anchors the faction that will become House Goratrix, the infernalist house that later forms the core of the Tremere antitribu within the Sabbat. For now, both Etrius and Goratrix still write to Meerlinda at Durham for counsel, each hoping she will take his side against the other; she gives it to neither, cautioning both instead to remember the blood and bonds that unite them against the clan's many outside enemies.

Meerlinda, the Tremere elder Ventrue chroniclers know as the Witch of Glastonbury, in fact maintains her working chantry from a tower near Durham Cathedral in northern England, ghouling apprentices such as young Geraint de Montfort to serve as companions and defenders of the site. From this remove she corresponds constantly with both Etrius at Ceoris and Goratrix in France, mediating — without much apparent hope of success — their deepening rivalry, while independently pursuing her own agenda against the Ventrue elder Mithras's repeated attempts to dislodge her from her claim at Glastonbury. Her Embrace of new childer follows the same ritual pattern used throughout the clan: infusion and exsanguination performed before a small gathering, sealed with an oath of loyalty to the pyramid rather than to any one elder. Her chantry's isolation in hostile, Church-dominated territory, and her success in holding it regardless, has made her something of a model for how a lone Tremere elder can carve out and defend a foothold far from Ceoris.

vtmlarp.source: Libellus Sanguinis II: Keepers of the Word, Book Two: Usurpers (Tremere)
